sp.p: By this fair heaven, I would have done it.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: [To himself] Oh, he swears admirably! "By this fair heaven," "Body of Caesar" — I shall never do it, sure. "Upon my salvation" — no, I have not the right grace.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: [Offering tobacco to Lorenzo Jr.] Signor, will you any? By this air, the most divine tobacco as ever I drunk.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: I thank you, sir.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: [To himself] Oh, this gentleman doth it rarely too, but nothing like the other. [He practices fencing at a post.] "By this air!" "As I am a gentleman!" "By Phoebus!"

l.seg: Master, glance, glance!

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: As I have a soul to be saved, I do protest —

p.seg: That you are a fool.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: [To Stephano] Cousin, will you any tobacco?

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: [Taking tobacco] Ay, sir, upon my salvation.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: How now, cousin?

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: I protest, as I am a gentleman, but no soldier, indeed.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: No, signor? As I remember, you served on a great horse last general muster.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Ay, sir, that's true. — Cousin, may I swear "as I am a soldier" by that?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Oh, yes, that you may.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Then, as I am a gentleman and a soldier, it is divine tobacco.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: But soft, where's Signor Matheo? Gone?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: No, sir, they went in here.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Oh, let’s follow them. Signor Matheo is gone to salute his mistress. [To Lorenzo Jr.] Sirrah, now thou shalt hear some of his verses, for he never comes hither without some shreds of poetry. — Come, Signor Stephano, Musco.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Musco? Where? Is this Musco?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Ay, but peace, cousin, no words of it at any hand.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Not I, by this fair heaven, as I have a soul to be saved, by Phoebus.

p.seg: Oh, rare! Your cousin's discourse is simply suited, all in oaths.
Ay, he lacks nothing but a little light stuff to draw them out withal, and he were rarely fitted to the time.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Ha! How many are there, sayest thou?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Marry, sir, your brother, Signor Prospero.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Tut, beside him: what strangers are there, man?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Strangers? Let me see: one, two — mass, I know not well, there's so many.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: How? So many?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Ay, there's some five or six of them at the most.

l.seg: A swarm, a swarm!
Spite of the devil, how they sting my heart! —

lg.l: How long hast thou been coming hither, Cob?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: But a little while, sir.

lg.l: Didst thou come running?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: No, sir.

lg.l: Tut, then, I am familiar with thy haste.

l.seg: Bane to my fortunes! What meant I to marry?
I that before was ranked in such content,
My mind attired in smooth, silken peace,
Being free master of mine own free thoughts,
And now become a slave? What, never sigh;
Be of good cheer, man, for thou art a cuckold.
'Tis done, 'tis done. Nay, when such flowing store,
Plenty itself, falls in my wife's lap,
The cornucopiae will be mine, I know.

lg.l: What entertainment had they? I am sure
My sister and my wife would bid them welcome, ha?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Like enough, yet I heard not a word of welcome.

l.seg: No, their lips were sealed with kisses, and the voice,
Drowned in a flood of joy at their arrival,
Had lost her motion, state, and faculty. —

lg.l: Cob, which of them was't that first kissed my wife?
My sister, I should say. My wife! Alas,
I fear not her. Ha? Who was it, say'st thou?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: By my troth, sir, will you have the truth of it?

lg.l: Oh, ay, good Cob, I pray thee.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: God's my judge, I saw nobody to be kissed, unless they would have kissed the post in the middle of the warehouse. For there I left them all at their tobacco — with a pox!

lg.l: How? Were they not gone in, then, ere thou cam'st?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Oh, no, sir.

lg.l: Spite of the devil! What do I stay here, then?
Cob, follow me.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Nay, soft and fair! I have eggs on the spit; I cannot go yet, sir. Now am I for some divers reasons hammering, hammering revenge. Oh, for three or four gallons of vinegar to sharpen my wits! Revenge, vinegar revenge, russet revenge! Nay, an he had not lain in my house, 'twould never have grieved me. But being my guest — one that, I'll be sworn, my wife has lent him her smock off her back while his own shirt ha' been at washing, pawned her neckerchers for clean bands for him, sold almost all my platters to buy him tobacco — and yet to see an ingratitude wretch strike his host! Well, I hope to raise up an host of Furies for't. Here comes Master Doctor.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What, 's Signor Thorello gone?

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Ay, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Heart of me, what made him leave us so abruptly? [Seeing Cob] How now, sirrah, what make you here? What would you have, ha?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: An't please Your Worship, I am a poor neighbor of Your Worship's.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: A neighbor of mine, knave?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Ay, sir, at the sign of the water-tankard, hard by the Green Lattice. I have paid scot and lot there any time this eighteen years.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What, at the Green Lattice?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: No, sir, to the parish. Marry, I have seldom scaped scot-free at the Lattice.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: So. But what business hath my neighbor?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: An't like Your Worship, I am come to crave the peace of Your Worship.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Of me, knave?. Peace of me, knave? Did I e'er hurt thee? Did I ever threaten thee? Or wrong thee? Ha?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: No, God's my comfort, I mean Your Worship's warrant for one that hath wronged me, sir. His arms are at too much liberty. I would fain have them bound to a treaty of peace, an I could by any means compass it.

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Why, dost thou go in danger of thy life for him?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: No, sir, but I go in danger of my death every hour by his means. An I die within a twelvemonth and a day, I may swear by the laws of the land that he killed me.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: How, how, knave? Swear he killed thee? What pretext, what color hast thou for that?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Marry, sir, both black and blue — color enough, I warrant you. I have it here to show Your Worship.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What is he that gave you this, sirrah?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: A gentleman in the city, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: A gentleman? What call you him?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Signor Bobadilla.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Good. But wherefore did he beat you, sirrah? How began the quarrel 'twixt you, ha? Speak truly, knave, I advise you.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Marry, sir, because I spake against their vagrant tobacco as I came by them; for nothing else.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Ha? You speak against tobacco? — Peto, his name.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: What's your name, sirrah?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Oliver Cob, sir. Set Oliver Cob, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To Peto] Tell Oliver Cob he shall go to the jail.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Oliver Cob, Master Doctor says you shall go to the jail.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Oh, I beseech Your Worship, for God's love, dear Master Doctor!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Nay, God's precious, an such drunken knaves as you are come to dispute of tobacco once, I have done. — Away with him!

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Oh, good Master Doctor! [To Lorenzo Sr.] Sweet gentleman!

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Sweet Oliver, would I could do thee any good. — Master Doctor, let me entreat, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What? A tankard-bearer, a threadbare rascal, a beggar, a slave that never drunk out of better than pisspot metal in his life? And he to deprave and abuse the virtue of an herb so generally received in the courts of princes, the chambers of nobles, the bowers of sweet ladies, the cabins of soldiers? Peto, away with him, by God's passion. I say, go to.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Dear Master Doctor!

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Alas, poor Oliver!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Peto, ay, and make him a warrant. — He shall not go; I but fear the knave.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Oh, divine doctor! Thanks, noble doctor, most dainty doctor, delicious doctor!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Signor Lorenzo, God's pity, man, be merry, be merry, leave these dumps.

lg.l: Troth, would I could, sir; but enforcd mirth,
In my weak judgment, has no happy birth.
The mind, being once a prisoner unto cares,
The more it dreams on joy, the worse it fares.
A smiling look is to a heavy soul
As a gilt bias to a leaden bowl,
Which in itself appears most vile, being spent
To no true use, but only for ostent.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Nay, but good signor, hear me a word, hear me a word. Your cares are nothing; they are like my cap, soon put on and as soon put off. What, your son is old enough to govern himself; let him run his course. It's the only way to make him a staid man. If he were an unthrift, a ruffian, a drunkard, or a licentious liver, then you had reason, you had reason to take care; but being none of these, God's passion, an I had twice so many cares as you have, I'd drown them all in a cup of sack. Come, come. I muse your parcel of a soldier returns not all this while.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Well, sister, I tell you true, and you'll find it so in the end.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Alas, brother, what would you have me to do? I cannot help it; you see, my brother Prospero, he brings them in here; they are his friends.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: His friends? His fiends! 'Sblood, they do nothing but haunt him up and down like a sort of unlucky sprites and tempt him to all manner of villainy that can be thought of. Well, by this light, a little thing would make me play the devil with some of them. An 'twere not more for your husband's sake than anything else, I'd make the house too hot for them. They should say and swear hell were broken loose ere they went. But, by God's bread, 'tis nobody's fault but yours. For, an you had done as you might have done, they should have been damned ere they should have come in, e'er a one of them!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: God's my life, did you ever hear the like? What a strange man is this! Could I keep out all them, think you? I should put myself against half a dozen men, should I? Good faith, you'd mad the patient'st body in the world to hear you talk so, without any sense or reason.

div2.stage: [Enter Matheo [holding papers], with Hesperida [and] Bobadilla, [followed at a distance by] Stephano, Lorenzo Jr., Prospero, [and] Musco.

lg.l: [To Matheo] Servant, in troth, you are too prodigal
Of your wit's treasure, thus to pour it forth
Upon so mean a subject as my worth.
You say well, you say well.
Hoyday, here is stuff!

p.seg: Oh, now stand close. Pray God she can get him to read it.
Tut, fear not. I warrant thee, he will do it of himself with much impudency.

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: [Indicating Matheo's papers] Servant, what is that same, I pray you?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Marry, an elegy, an elegy, an odd toy.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Ay, to mock an ape withal. O Jesu!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Sister, I pray you, let's hear it.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Mistress, I'll read it, if you please.

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: I pray you do, servant.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Oh, here's no foppery! 'Sblood, it frets me to the gall to think on it.

p.seg: Oh, ay, it is his condition. Peace, we are fairly rid of him.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Faith, I did it in an humor. I know not how it is, but, please you, come near, signor. This gentleman [indicating Stephano] hath judgment; 1537he knows how to censure of a — [To Stephano] I pray you, sir, you can judge.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Not I, sir — as I have a soul to be saved; as I am a gentleman.

p.seg: Nay, it's well, so long as he doth not forswear himself.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: [To Matheo] Signor, you abuse the excellency of your mistress and her fair sister. Fie, while you live, avoid this prolixity.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: I shall, sir. Well, incipere dulce .

p.seg: How? "Insipere dulce" ? "A sweet thing to be a fool," indeed.

l.seg: What, do you take "incipere" in that sense?

p.seg: You do not, you? 'Sblood, this was your villainy, to gull him with a mot.
Oh, the benchers' phrase: pauca verba, pauca verba .

lg.l: [Reads] Rare creature, let me speak without offense.
Would God my rude words had the influence
To rule thy thoughts, as thy fair looks do mine!
Then shouldst thou be his prisoner who is thine.

p.seg: 'Sheart, this is in Hero and Leander!

l.seg: Oh, ay, peace. We shall have more of this.

lg.l: [Reciting] Be not unkind and fair. Misshapen stuff
Is of behavior boisterous and rough —

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Stephano] How like you that, signor?

div2.stage: [Stephano shakes his head vigorously up and down.]

lg.l: [Aside to Prospero] 'Sblood, he shakes his head like a bottle, to feel an there be any brain in it.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: But observe the catastrophe now:

lg.l: And I in duty will exceed all other
As you in beauty do excel Love's mother.

p.seg: Well, I'll have him free of the brokers, for he utters nothing but stol'n remnants.
Nay, good critic, forbear.
A pox on him, hang him, filching rogue! Steal from the dead? It's worse than sacrilege.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Hesperida] Sister, what have you here? Verses? I pray you, let's see.

div2.stage: [Prospero takes the verses from Hesperida and examines them.]

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Do you let them go so lightly, sister?

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: Yes, faith, when they come lightly.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Ay, but if your servant should hear you, he would take it heavily.

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: No matter. He is able to bear.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: So are asses.

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: So is he.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Signor Matheo, who made these verses? They are excellent good.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Oh, God, sir, it's your pleasure to say so, sir. Faith, I made them extempore this morning.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: How, extempore?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: I would I might be damned else. Ask Signor Bobadilla. He saw me write them at the — pox on it! — the Miter yonder.

p.seg: Well, an the Pope knew he cursed the miter, it were enough to have him excommunicated all the taverns in the town.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: [To Lorenzo Jr.] Cousin, how do you like this gentleman's verses?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Oh, admirable! The best that ever I heard.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: By this fair heavens, they are admirable, the best that ever I heard.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To himself] I am vexed. I can hold never a bone of me still! 'Sblood, I think they mean to build a tabernacle here. Well!

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Hesperida] Sister, you have a simple servant here, that crowns your beauty with such encomions and devices. You may see what it is to be the mistress of a wit that can make your perfections so transparent that every blear eye may look through them and see him drowned over head and ears in the deep well of desire. — Sister Bianca, I marvel you get you not a servant that can rhyme and do tricks, too.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To himself] Oh, monster! Impudence itself! Tricks?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: [To Prospero] Tricks, brother? What tricks?

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: Nay, speak, I pray you, what tricks?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Ay, never spare anybody here, but say, what tricks?

lg.l: Passion of my heart! "Do tricks"?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: 'Sblood, here's a trick, vied and revied. Why, you monkeys, you, what a caterwauling do you keep! Has he not given you rhymes and verses and tricks?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To himself] Oh, see the devil!

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Hesperida] Nay, you lamp of virginity, that take it in snuff so, come and cherish this tame poetical fury in your "servant"; you'll be begged else shortly for a concealment. Go to, reward his muse. You cannot give him less than a shilling, in conscience, for the book he had it out of cost him a teston at the least. — How now, gallants, Lorenzo, Signor Bobadilla? What, all sons of silence? No spirit?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [Aloud] Come, you might practice your ruffian tricks somewhere else and not here, iwis. This is no tavern, nor no place for such exploits.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: 'Sheart, how now?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Nay, boy, never look askance at me for the matter. I'll tell you of it, by God's bread! Ay, and you and your companions, mend yourselves when I have done.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: My companions?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Ay, your companions, sir, so I say. 'Sblood, I am not afraid of you nor them neither. You must have your poets and your cavaliers and your fools follow you up and down the city, and here they must come to domineer and swagger? [To Matheo] Sirrah, you ballad-singer, and Slops, your fellow there, get you out! Get you out or, by the will of God, I'll cut off your ears! Go to.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO

lg.l: [To Matheo and Bobadilla, as they move away] 'Sblood, stay. Let's see what he dare do.

sp.p: [To Giuliano] Cut off his ears? You are an ass. Touch any man here and, by the Lord, I'll run my rapier to the hilts in thee.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Yea, that would I fain see, boy.

div2.stage: They all draw. The women make a great cry.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Oh, Jesu! Piso, Matheo, murder!

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: Help, help, Piso!

div2.stage: [Enter Piso and some more of the house to part them.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Gentlemen! Prospero! Forbear, I pray you.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: [To Giuliano] Well, sirrah, you Holofernes: by my hand, I will pink thy flesh full of holes with my rapier for this, I will, by this good heaven! They offer to fight again and are parted. Nay, let him come, let him come, gentlemen; by the body of Saint George, I'll not kill him.

sp.speaker: PISO
sp.p: Hold, hold! Forbear.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To Bobadilla] You whoreson bragging coistrel!

lg.l: Why, how now? What's the matter? What stir is here?
Whence springs this quarrel? Piso! Where is he? —
Put up your weapons and put off this rage.
My wife and sister, they are cause of this. —
What, Piso! — Where is this knave?

sp.speaker: PISO
sp.p: Here, sir.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Lorenzo Jr.. and the others] Come, let's go. This is one of my brother's ancient humors, this.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: I am glad nobody was hurt by this ancient humor.

div2.stage: Exeunt Prospero, Lorenzo Jr., Musco, Stephano, Bobadilla, [and] Matheo.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Why, how now, brother, who enforced this brawl?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: A sort of lewd rakehells, that care neither for God nor the devil. And they must come here to read ballads and roguery and trash! I'll mar the knot of them ere I sleep, perhaps, especially Signor Pythagoras, he that's all manner of shapes, and Songs and Sonnets, his fellow there.

lg.l: Brother, indeed, you are too violent,
Too sudden in your courses; and you know
My brother Prospero's temper will not bear
Any reproof, chiefly in such a presence
Where every slight disgrace he should receive
Would wound him in opinion and respect.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Respect? What talk you of respect 'mongst such as had neither spark of manhood nor good manners? By God, I am ashamed to hear you. Respect?

lg.l: Yes, there was one, a civil gentleman,
And very worthily demeaned himself.
Oh, that was some love of yours, sister.
A love of mine? In faith, I would he were
No other's love but mine.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Indeed, he seemed to be a gentleman of an exceeding fair disposition and of very excellent good parts.

l.seg: Her love, by Jesu! My wife's minion!
"Fair disposition"? "Excellent good parts"?
'Sheart , these phrases are intolerable.
"Good parts"? How should she know his parts? Well, well,
It is too plain, too clear. —

lg.l: What, are they gone?
Ay, sir, they went in.
Are any of the gallants within?
No, sir, they are all gone.
Art thou sure of it?
Ay, sir, I can assure you.
Piso, what gentleman was that they praised so?
One they call him Signor Lorenzo, a fair young gentleman, sir.

l.seg: Ay, I thought so; my mind gave me as much.
'Sblood, I'll be hanged if they have not hid him in the house
Somewhere! I'll go search. —

lg.l: Be true to me and thou shalt find me bountiful.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: [Knocking] What, Tib! Tib, I say!

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: [Within] How now, what cuckold is that knocks so hard? (To him, Tib.) Oh, husband, is't you? What's the news?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Nay, you have stunned me, i'faith! You have given me a knock on the forehead will stick by me. Cuckold? 'Swounds, cuckold?

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: Away, you fool! Did I know it was you that knocked? Come, come, you may call me as bad when you list.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: May I? 'Swounds, Tib, you are a whore.

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: 'Sheart, you lie in your throat.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: How, the lie? And in my throat too? Do you long to be stabbed, ha?

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: Why, you are no soldier.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Mass, that's true. When was Bobadilla here? That rogue, that slave, that fencing Burgullian! I'll tickle him, i'faith.

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: Why, what's the matter?

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Oh, he hath basted me rarely, sumptuously! But I have it here will sauce him. Oh, the doctor, the honestest old Trojan in all Italy! I do honor the very flea of his dog. A plague on him, he put me once in a villainous, filthy fear. Marry, it vanished away like the smoke of tobacco, but I was smoked soundly first, I thank the devil and his good angel, my guest. Well, wife, or Tib, which you will, get you in and lock the door, I charge you, let no body in to you — not Bobadilla himself, nor the devil in his likeness. You are a woman; you have flesh and blood enough in you; therefore, be not tempted; keep the door shut upon all comers.

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: I warrant you, there shall no body enter here without my consent.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Nor with your consent, sweet Tib; and so I leave you.

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: It's more than you know, whether you leave me so.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: How?

lg.l: Why, sweet.
Tut, sweet or sour, thou art a flower.
Keep close thy door. I ask no more.

div2.stage: [Enter Lorenzo Jr., Prospero, Stephano, [and] Musco [disguised still as a soldier. Lorenzo Jr., Prospero, and Musco confer where Stephano cannot hear them.]

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Well, Musco, perform this business happily and thou makest a conquest of my love forever.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Musco] I'faith, now let thy spirits put on their best habit. But, at any hand, remember thy message to my brother, for there's no other means to start him.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I warrant you, sir, fear nothing. I have a nimble soul that hath waked all my imaginative forces by this time and put them in true motion. What you have possessed me withal, I'll discharge it amply, sir. Make no question.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: That's well said, Musco. Exit Musco. [To Lorenzo Jr.] Faith, sirrah, how dost thou approve my wit in this device?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Troth, well, howsoever, but excellent if it take.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Take, man? Why, it cannot choose but take, if the circumstances miscarry not. But tell me zealously: dost thou affect my sister Hesperida, as thou pretendest?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Prospero, by Jesu!

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Come, do not protest, I believe thee. I'faith, she is a virgin of good ornament and much modesty. Unless I conceived very worthily of her, thou shouldst not have her.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Nay, I think it a question whether I shall have her, for all that.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: 'Sblood, thou shalt have her, by this light thou shalt.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Nay, do not swear.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: By Saint Mark, thou shalt have her. I'll go fetch her presently. Point but where to meet, and, by this hand, I'll bring her.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Hold, hold. What, all policy dead? No prevention of mischiefs stirring?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Why, by — what shall I swear by? Thou shalt have her, by my soul.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: I pray thee, have patience. I am satisfied. Prospero, omit no offered occasion that may make my desires complete, I beseech thee.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: I warrant thee.

div2.stage: [Enter Lorenzo Sr. [and] Peto, meeting Musco [still disguised as a soldier].

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Was your man a soldier, sir?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Ay, a knave. I took him up begging upon the way, this morning as I was coming to the city.

lg.l: Oh, here he is. — Come on, you make fair speed.
Why, where on God's name have you been so long?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Marry, God's my comfort, where I thought I should have had little comfort of Your Worship's service.

lg.l: How so?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Oh, God, sir! Your coming to the city, and your entertainment of me, and your sending me to watch — indeed, all the circumstances are as open to your son as to yourself.

lg.l: How should that be? Unless that villain Musco
Have told him of the letter and discovered
All that I strictly charged him to conceal? 'Tis so.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I'faith, you have hit it; 'tis so, indeed.

lg.l: But how should he know thee to be my man?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Nay, sir, I cannot tell, unless it were by the black art. Is not your son a scholar, sir?

lg.l: Yes, but I hope his soul is not allied
To such a devilish practice. If it were,
I had just cause to weep my part in him
And curse the time of his creation.
But where didst thou find them, Portensio?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Nay, sir, rather you should ask where they found me, for I'll be sworn I was going along in the street, thinking nothing, when of a sudden one calls, "Signor Lorenzo's man!" Another, he cries, "Soldier!" And thus half a dozen of them, till they had got me within doors, where I no sooner came but out flies their rapiers and, all bent against my breast, they swore some two or three hundred oaths, and all to tell me I was but a dead man if I did not confess where you were, and how I was employed, and about what. Which, when they could not get out of me — as God's my judge, they should have killed me first — they locked me up into a room in the top of a house, where by great miracle, having a light heart, I slid down by a bottom of packthread into the street and so scaped. But master, thus much I can assure you, for I heard it while I was locked up: there were a great many merchants and rich citizens' wives with them at a banquet, and your son, Signor Lorenzo, has pointed one of them to meet anon at one Cob's house, a waterbearer's, that dwells by the wall. Now there you shall be sure to take him, for fail he will not.

lg.l: Nor will I fail to break this match, I doubt not.
Well, go thou along with Master Doctor's man,
And stay there for me. At one Cob's house, say'st thou?

p.seg: When, can you tell? Much wench or much son! 'Sblood, when he has stayed there three or four hours, travailing with the expectation of somewhat, and at the length be delivered of nothing — oh, the sport that I should then take to look on him if I durst! But now I mean to appear no more afore him in this shape; I have another trick to act yet. Oh, that I were so happy as to light upon an ounce now of this doctor's clerk!

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: I thank you, good sir.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I have made you stay somewhat long, sir.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Not a whit, sir. I pray you, what, sir, do you mean? You have been lately in the wars, sir, it seems.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Ay, marry, have I, sir.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Troth, sir, I would be glad to bestow a pottle of wine of you, if it please you to accept it —

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Oh, Lord, sir!

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: But to hear the manner of your services and your devices in the wars. They say they be very strange, and not like those a man reads in the Roman histories.

p.seg: And more too, somewhat.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: No better time than now, sir. We'll go to the Mermaid. There we shall have a cup of neat wine. I pray you, sir, let me request you.

p.seg: He is mine own, i'faith.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: [To Lorenzo Jr.] Signor, did you ever see the like clown of him where we were today, Signor Prospero's brother? I think the whole earth cannot show his like, by Jesu.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: We were now speaking of him. Signor Bobadilla tells me he is fallen foul of you two.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Oh, ay, sir, he threatened me with the bastinado .

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Ay, but I think I taught you a trick this morning for that. You shall kill him, without all question, if you be so minded.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Indeed, it is a most excellent trick.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Oh, you do not give spirit enough to your motion. You are too dull, too tardy. Oh, it must be done like lightning. Hay!

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Oh, rare!

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Tut, 'tis nothing, an't be not done in a — .

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Signor, did you never play with any of our masters here?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Oh, good sir!

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Nay, for a more instance of their preposterous humor, there came three or four of them to me at a gentleman's house, where it was my chance to be resident at that time, to entreat my presence at their schools, and withal so much importuned me that — I protest to you, as I am a gentleman — I was ashamed of their rude demeanor out of all measure. Well, I told them that to come to a public school, they should pardon me, it was opposite to my humor; but if so they would attend me at my lodging, I protested to do them what right or favor I could, as I was a gentleman, et cetera -

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: So, sir, then you tried their skill?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Alas, soon tried! You shall hear, sir. Within two or three days after, they came, and, by Jesu, good signor, believe me, I graced them exceedingly, showed them some two or three tricks of prevention hath got them since admirable credit. They cannot deny this. And yet now they hate me; and why? Because I am excellent, and for no other reason on the earth.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: This is strange and vile as ever I heard.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: I will tell you, sir. Upon my first coming to the city they assaulted me, some three, four, five, six of them together, as I have walked alone in divers places of the city, as upon the Exchange, at my lodging, and at my ordinary, where I have driven them afore me the whole length of a street in the open view of all our gallants, pitying to hurt them, believe me. Yet all this lenity will not depress their spleen; they will be doing with the pismire, raising a hill a man may spurn abroad with his foot at pleasure. By my soul, I could have slain them all, but I delight not in murder. I am loath to bear any other but a bastinado for them, and yet I hold it good policy not to go disarmed, for, though I be skillful, I may be suppressed with multitudes.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Ay, by Jesu, may you, sir, and in my conceit our whole nation should sustain the loss by it, if it were so.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Alas, no. What's a peculiar man to a nation? Not seen.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Ay, but your skill, sir.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Indeed, that might be some loss, but who respects it? I will tell you, signor, in private: I am a gentleman and live here obscure and to myself. But were I known to the duke, observe me, I would undertake, upon my head and life, for the public benefit of the state, not only to spare the entire lives of his subjects in general, but to save the one half — nay, three parts — of his yearly charges in holding wars generally against all his enemies. And how will I do it, think you?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Nay, I know not, nor can I conceive.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Marry, thus: I would select nineteen more to myself throughout the land; gentlemen they should be of good spirit, strong and able constitution. I would choose them by an instinct, a trick that I have. And I would teach these nineteen the special tricks — as your punto , your reverso , your stoccato , your imbroccato , your passado , your montanto — till they could all play very near or altogether as well as myself. This done, say the enemy were forty thousand strong: we twenty would come into the field the tenth of March or thereabouts and would challenge twenty of the enemy. They could not in their honor refuse the combat. Well, we would kill them; challenge twenty more, kill them; twenty more, kill them; twenty more, kill them too. And thus would we kill every man his twenty a day, that's twenty score; twenty score, that's two hundred; two hundred a day, five days a thousand. Forty thousand — forty times five, five times forty — two hundred days kills them all, by computation. And this will I venture my life to perform, provided there by no treason practiced upon us.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Why, are you so sure of your hand at all times?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Tut, never mistrust, upon my soul.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Mass, I would not stand in Signor Giuliano's state, then, an you meet him, for the wealth of Florence.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Why, signor, by Jesu, if he were here now, I would not draw my weapon on him. Let this gentleman do his mind, but I will bastinado him , by heaven, an ever I meet him.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Faith, and I'll have a fling at him.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Look, yonder he goes, I think.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To himself] 'Sblood, what luck have I! I cannot meet with these bragging rascals.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: It's not he, is it?

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Yes, faith, it is he.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: I'll be hanged, then, if that were he.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Before God, it was he. You make me swear.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Upon my salvation, it was he.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Well, had I thought it had been he, he could not have gone so. But I cannot be induced to believe it was he yet.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To Bobadilla] Oh, gallant, have I found you? Draw. To your tools! Draw! Or, by God's will, I'll thrash you.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Signor, hear me!

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Draw your weapons, then.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Signor, I never thought on it till now: body of Saint George, I have a warrant of the peace served on me even now as I came along, by a waterbearer. This gentleman saw it — Signor Matheo.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: The peace? 'Sblood, you will not draw?

div2.stage: He beats him and disarms him.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Hold, signor, hold! Under thy favor, forbear!

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To Bobadilla] Prate again as you like this, you whoreson cowardly rascal! You'll control the point, you? Your consort, he is gone? Had he stayed, he had shared with you, in faith.

div2.stage: Exit Giuliano [leaving his cloak] behind him in his haste].

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Well, gentlemen, bear witness I was bound to the peace, by Jesu.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Why, and though you were, sir, the law allows you to defend yourself. That's but a poor excuse.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: I cannot tell. I never sustained the like disgrace, by heaven. Sure I was struck with a planet then, for I had no power to touch my weapon.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Ay, like enough. I have heard of many that have been beaten under a planet. Go, get you to the surgeon's. 'Sblood, an these be your tricks, your passados and your montantos , I'll none of them. Exit [Bobadilla]. Oh, God, that this age should bring forth such creatures! — Come, cousin.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: [Taking up Giuliano's cloak] Mass, I'll have this cloak.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: God's will, it's Giuliano's.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Nay, but 'tis mine now; another might have ta'en it up as well as I. I'll wear it, so I will.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: How an he see it? He'll challenge it, assure yourself.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Ay, but he shall not have it. I'll say I bought it.

sp.speaker: LORENZO JR.
sp.p: Advise you, cousin, take heed he give not you as much.

lg.l: Now trust me, Prospero, you were much to blame
T'incense your brother and disturb the peace
Of my poor house; for there be sentinels
That every minute watch to give alarums
Of civil war, without adjection
Of your assistance and occasion.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: No harm done, brother, I warrant you. Since there is no harm done, anger costs a man nothing, and a tall man is never his own man till he be angry. To keep his valor in obscurity is to keep himself, as it were, in a cloakbag. What's a musician unless he play? What's a tall man unless he fight? For, indeed, all this my brother stands upon absolutely, and that made me fall in with him so resolutely.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Ay, but what harm might have come of it!

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Might? So might the good warm clothes your husband wears be poisoned, for anything he knows, or the wholesome wine he drunk even now at the table.

l.seg: Oh, me, now I remember:
My wife drunk to me last and changed the cup,
And bade me wear this cursd suit today.
See if God suffer murder undiscovered! —

lg.l: I feel me ill. Give me some mithridate;
Some mithridate and oil, good sister, fetch me.
Oh, I am sick at heart! I burn, I burn.
If you will save my life, go fetch it me.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Oh, strange humor! My very breath hath poisoned him.

lg.l: [To Thorello] Good brother, be content. What do you mean?
The strength of these extreme conceits will kill you.
Beshrew your heart-blood, brother Prospero,
For putting such a toy into his head!

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Is a fit simile a toy? Will he be poisoned with a simile? — Brother Thorello, what a strange and vain imagination is this! For shame, be wiser. Of my soul, there's no such matter.

lg.l: Am I not sick? How am I then not poisoned?
Am I not poisoned? How am I then so sick?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: If you be sick, your own thoughts make you sick.

lg.l: His jealousy is the poison he hath taken.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Signor Thorello, my master, Doctor Clement, salutes you and desires to speak with you with all speed possible.

p.seg: I'll seek them out and set them sentinels till I return.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [Privately to Musco] Musco, this is rare. But how got'st thou this apparel of the Doctor's man?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Marry, sir, my youth would needs bestow the wine of me to hear some martial discourse, where I so marshalled him that I made him monstrous drunk. And because too much heat was the cause of his distemper, I stripped him stark naked, as he lay along asleep, and borrowed his suit to deliver this counterfeit message in, leaving a rusty armor and an old brown bill to watch him till my return — which shall be when I have pawned his apparel and spent the money, perhaps.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Well, thou art a mad knave, Musco. His absence will be a good subject for more mirth. I pray thee, return to thy young master Lorenzo and will him to meet me and Hesperida at the Friary presently; for here, tell him, the house is so stirred with jealousy that there is no room for love to stand upright in. But I'll use such means she shall come thither, and that, I think, will meet best with his desires. Hie thee, good Musco.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I go, sir.

div2.stage: [Enter Thorello [unaware of the presence of Bianca and Prospero].

lg.l: Ho, Piso! Cob! Where are these villains, trow?
Oh, art thou there? Piso, hark thee here;
Mark what I say to thee. I must go forth.
Be careful of thy promise. Keep good watch;
Note every gallant, and observe him well,
That enters in my absence to thy mistress.
If she would show him rooms, the jest is stale.
Follow them, Piso, or else hang on him,
And let him not go after. Mark their looks;
Note if she offer but to see his band
Or any other amorous toy about him.
But praise his leg or foot, or if she say
The day is hot, and bid him feel her hand,
How hot it is — oh, that's a monstrous thing!
Note me all this, sweet Piso; mark their sighs,
And if they do but whisper, break them off.
I'll bear thee out in it. Wilt thou do this?
Wilt thou be true, sweet Piso?

sp.speaker: PISO
sp.p: Most true, sir.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Thanks, gentle Piso. Where is Cob, now? — Cob!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: He's ever calling for Cob. I wonder how he employs Cob so.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Indeed, sister, to ask how he employs Cob is a necessary question for you that are his wife and a thing not very easy for you to be satisfied in. But this I'll assure you: Cob's wife is an excellent bawd, indeed, and oftentimes your husband haunts her house — marry, to what end I cannot altogether accuse him. Imagine you what you think convenient. But I have known fair hides have foul hearts ere now, I can tell you.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Never said you truer than that, brother. — Piso, fetch your cloak and go with me; I'll after him presently. I would to Christ I could take him there, i'faith!

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: So, let them go. This may make sport anon. — Now, my fair sister Hesperida: ah, that you knew how happy a thing it were to be fair and beautiful!

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: That toucheth not me, brother.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: That's true; that's even the fault of it. For, indeed, beauty stands a woman in no stead unless it procure her touching. But sister, whether it touch you or no, it touches your beauties, and I am sure they will abide the touch. An they do not, a plague of all ceruse, say I! And it touches me too in part, though not in the —. Well, there's a dear and respected friend of mine, sister, stands very strongly affected towards you, and hath vowed to inflame whole bonfires of zeal in his heart in honor of your perfections. I have already engaged my promise to bring you where you shall hear him confirm much more than I am able to lay down for him. Signor Lorenzo is the man. What say you, sister? Shall I entreat so much favor of you for my friend as to direct and attend you to his meeting? Upon my soul, he loves you extremely. Approve it, sweet Hesperida, will you?

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: Faith, I had very little confidence in mine own constancy if I durst not meet a man. But brother Prospero, this motion of yours savors of an old knight-adventurer's servant, methinks.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: What's that, sister?

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: Marry, of the squire.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: No matter, Hesperida, if it did. I would be such an one for my friend. But say, will you go?

sp.speaker: HESPERIDA
sp.p: Brother, I will, and bless my happy stars.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, what villainy is this? My man gone on a false message, and run away when he has done? Why, what trick is there in it, trow?

lg.l: How? Is my wife gone forth? Where is she, sister?
She's gone abroad with Piso.
Abroad with Piso? Oh, that villain dors me!
He hath discovered all unto my wife.
Beast that I was to trust him! Whither went she?
I know not, sir.
I'll tell you, brother, whither I suspect she's gone.
Whither, for God's sake?
To Cob's house, I believe; but keep my counsel.
I will, I will. To Cob's house? Doth she haunt Cob's?
She's gone o'purpose now to cuckold me
With that lewd rascal, who, to win her favor,
Hath told her all.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To Hesperida] But did you, mistress, see my man bring him a message?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: That we did, Master Doctor.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: And whither went the knave?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: To the tavern, I think, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What, did Thorello give him anything to spend for the message he brought him? If he did, I should commend my man's wit exceedingly if he would make himself drunk with the joy of it. Farewell, lady. Keep good rule, you two, I beseech you now. By God's marry, my man makes me laugh!

lg.l: What a mad doctor this is! Come, sister, let's away.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: I wonder, signor, what they will say of my going away, ha?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Why, what should they say, but as of a discreet gentleman, quick, wary, respectful of nature's fair lineaments, and that's all?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Why, so, but what can they say of your beating?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: A rude part, a touch with soft wood, a kind of gross battery used, laid on strongly, borne most patiently, and that's all.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Ay, but would any man have offered it in Venice?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Tut, I assure you, no. You shall have there your nobilis , your gentilezza , come in bravely upon your reverse, stand you close, stand you firm, stand you fair, save your retricato with his left leg, come to the assalto with the right, thrust with brave steel, defy your base wood. But wherefore do I awake this remembrance? I was bewitched, by Jesu! But I will be revenged.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Do you hear? Is't not best to get a warrant, and have him arrested and brought before Doctor Clement?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: It were not amiss. Would we had it!

div2.stage: [Enter Musco [disguised as Peto, the Doctor's clerk].

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Why, here comes his man. Let's speak to him.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Agreed. Do you speak.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: [To Musco] God save you, sir.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: With all my heart, sir.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Sir, there is one Giuliano hath abused this gentleman and me, and we determine to make our amends by law. Now, if you would do us the favor to procure us a warrant for his arrest of your master, you shall be well considered, I assure, i'faith, sir.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Sir, you know my service is my living. Such favors as these gotten of my master is his only preferment, and therefore you must consider me as I may make benefit of my place.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: How is that?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Faith, sir, the thing is extraordinary, and the gentleman may be of great account. Yet, be what he will, if you will lay me down five crowns in my hand, you shall have it; otherwise, not.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: How shall we do, signor? You have no money?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Not a cross, by Jesu.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Nor I, before God, but two pence, left of my two shillings in the morning for wine and cakes. Let's give him some pawn.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Pawn? We have none to the value of his demand.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Oh, Lord, man, I'll pawn this jewel in my ear, and you may pawn your silk stockings, and pull up your boots. They will ne'er be missed.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Well, an there be no remedy, I'll step aside and put them off.

div2.stage: [He removes his stockings. Matheo removes his earring.]

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: [To Musco] Do you hear, sir? We have no store of money at this time, but you shall have good pawns — look you, sir, this jewel and this gentleman's silk stockings — because we would have it dispatched ere we went to our chambers.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I am content, sir. I will get you the warrant presently. What's his name, say you? Giuliano?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Ay, ay, Giuliano.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: What manner of man is he?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: A tall, big man, sir. He goes in a cloak most commonly of silk russet, laid about with russet lace.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: 'Tis very good, sir.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Here, sir, here's my jewel.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: And here are stockings.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Well, gentlemen, I'll procure this warrant presently and appoint you a varlet of the city to serve it. If you'll be upon the Rialto anon, the varlet shall meet you there.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Very good, sir. I wish no better.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: This is rare! Now will I go pawn this cloak of the Doctor's man at the broker's for a varlet's suit, and be the varlet myself, and get either more pawns or more money of Giuliano for my arrest.

lg.l: Oh, here it is. I am glad I have found it now.
[He knocks.] Ho! Who is within here?
I am within, sir. What's your pleasure?
To know who is within besides yourself.
Why, sir, you are no constable, I hope?
Oh, fear you the constable? Then I doubt not
You have some guests within deserve that fear.
I'll fetch him straight.
I'God's name, sir!
Go to. Tell me, is not the young Lorenzo here?
Young Lorenzo? I saw none such, sir, of mine honesty.
Go to, your honesty flies too lightly from you.
There's no way but fetch the constable.
The constable? The man is mad, I think.

div2.stage: Claps to the door. [Lorenzo Sr. starts to leave.]
[Enter Piso and Bianca. [Lorenzo Sr. stands aside, unseen by them.]

lg.l: Ho! Who keeps house here?

l.seg: Oh, this is the female copesmate of my son.
Now shall I meet him straight.

lg.l: Knock, Piso, pray thee.
[Knocking] Ho, good wife!
[Within] Why, what's the matter with you?
Why, woman, grieves it you to ope your door?
Belike you get something to keep it shut.
What mean these questions, pray ye?
So strange you make it?
Is not Thorello, my tried husband, here?

l.seg: Her husband?

lg.l: I hope he needs not to be tried here.
No, dame, he doth it not for need, but pleasure.
Neither for need nor pleasure is he here.

l.seg: This is but a device to balk me withal. Soft, who's this?

lg.l: Oh, sir, have I forestalled your honest market?
Found your close walks? You stand amazed now, do you?
I'faith, I am glad I have smoked you yet at last.
What's your jewel, trow? In, come, let's see her.
[To Tib] Fetch forth your huswife, dame! [To Thorello] If she be fairer,
In any honest judgment, than myself,
I'll be content with it. But she is change,
She feeds you fat, she soothes your appetite,
And you are well? Your wife, an honest woman,
Is meat twice sod to you, sir? Ah, you treacher!

l.seg: She cannot counterfeit this palpably.

lg.l: [To Bianca] Out on thee, more than strumpet's impudency!
Steal'st thou thus to thy haunts? And have I taken
Thy bawd and thee and thy companion,
This hoary-headed lecher, this old goat,
Close at your villainy? And wouldst thou 'scuse it
With this stale harlot's jest, accusing me?
[To Lorenzo Sr.] Oh, old incontinent, dost thou not shame,
When all thy powers' inchastity is spent,
To have a mind so hot, and to entice
And feed the enticements of a lustful woman?
Out! I defy thee, I, dissembling wretch!
Defy me, strumpet? [He points to Piso.] Ask thy pander here.
Can he deny it? [He points to Lorenzo Sr.] Or that wicked elder?
Why, hear you, signor —
Tut, tut, never speak.
Thy guilty conscience will discover thee.
What lunacy is this that haunts this man?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Oh, sister, did you see my cloak?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Not I, I see none.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: God's life, I have lost it, then. Saw you Hesperida?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Hesperida? Is she not at home?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: No, she is gone abroad, and nobody can tell me of it at home.

lg.l: O heaven! Abroad? What, light? A harlot too?
Why, why? Hark you, hath she, hath she not a brother,
A brother's house to keep, to look unto,
But she must fling abroad? My wife hath spoiled her.
She takes right after her; she does, she does.
[To Tib] Well, you goody bawd and —
lg.stage: [Enter Cob [unobserved at first by the others].
lg.l: That make your husband such a hoddy-doddy!
[To Piso and Lorenzo Sr.] And you, young apple-squire, and old cuckold-maker,
I'll have you every one before the Doctor.
Nay, you shall answer it. I charge you, go.
Marry, with all my heart; I'll go willingly.
How have I wronged myself in coming here!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: [To Thorello] Go with thee? I'll go with thee to thy shame, I warrant thee.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Why, what's the matter? What's here to do?

lg.l: [Seeing Cob] What, Cob, art thou here? Oh, I am abused,
And in thy house. Was never man so wronged!
'Slid, in my house? Who wronged you in my house?
Marry, young-lust-in-old and old-in-young, here.
Thy wife's their bawd; here have I taken them.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: [To Tib] Do you hear? Did I not charge you keep your doors shut here, and do you let them lie open for all comers? (Cob beats his wife.) [She fights back.] Do you scratch?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Friend, have patience. If she have done wrong in this, let her answer it before the magistrate.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: [To Tib] Ay, come, you shall go afore the Doctor.

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: Nay, I will go. I'll see an you may be allowed to beat your poor wife thus at every cuckoldly knave's pleasure. The devil and the pox take you all for me! Why do you not go now?

lg.l: A bitter quean. Come, we'll have you tamed.

div2.stage: [Enter Musco alone [wearing the gown and carrying the mace of a "varlet" or arresting officer].

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Well, of all my disguises yet, now am I most like myself, being in this varlet's suit. A man of my present profession never counterfeits till he lay hold upon a debtor and says he 'rests him, for then he brings him to all manner of unrest. A kind of little kings we are, bearing the diminutive of a mace made like a young artichoke that always carries pepper and salt in itself. Well, I know not what danger I undergo by this exploit. Pray God I come well off.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: See, I think yonder is the varlet.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Let's go in quest of him.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: [To Musco] God save you, friend. Are not you here by the appointment of Doctor Clement's man?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Yes, an please you, sir. He told me two gentlemen had willed him to procure an arrest upon one Signor Giuliano by a warrant from his master, which I have about me.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: It is honestly done of you both. And see where he comes you must arrest. Upon him, for God's sake, before he be ware!

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Bear back, Matheo!

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Signor Giuliano, I arrest you, sir, in the duke's name.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Signor Giuliano? Am I Signor Giuliano? I am one Signor Stephano, I tell you, and you do not well, by God's lid, to arrest me, I tell you truly. I am not in your master's books, I would you should well know. Ay, and a plague of God on you for making me afraid thus!

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Why, how are you deceived, gentlemen!

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: He wears such a cloak, and that deceived us. But see, here 'a comes. Officer, this is he.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To Stephano] Why, how now, Signor Gull, are you turned filcher of late? Come, deliver my cloak.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Your cloak, sir? I bought it even now in the market.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Signor Giuliano, I must arrest you, sir.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Arrest me, sir? At whose suit?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: At these two gentlemen's.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: I obey thee, varlet; but for these villains —

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Keep the peace, I charge you, sir, in the duke's name, sir.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: What's the matter, varlet?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: You must go before Master Doctor Clement, sir, to answer what these gentlemen will object against you. Hark you, sir, I will use you kindly.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: [To Giuliano] We'll be even with you, sir. — Come, Signor Bobadilla, we'll go before and prepare the Doctor. — Varlet, look to him.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: The varlet is a tall man, by Jesu.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Away, you rascals! Exeunt Bobadilla and Matheo. [To Stephano] Signor, I shall have my cloak.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Your cloak? I say once again I bought it, and I'll keep it.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: You will keep it?

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Ay, that I will.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [To Musco] Varlet, stay! Here's thy fee. Arrest him.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Signor Stephano, I arrest you.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Arrest me? There, take your cloak; I'll none of it.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Nay, that shall not serve your turn. — Varlet, bring him away. I'll go with thee now to the Doctor's. And carry him along.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Why, is not here your cloak? What would you have?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: I care not for that.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I pray you, sir.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Never talk of it. I will have him answer it.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Well, sir, then I'll leave you. I'll take this gentleman's word for his appearance, as I have done yours.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Tut, I'll have no words taken. Bring him along to answer it.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Good sir, I pity the gentleman's case. Here's your money again.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: God's bread, tell not me of my money. Bring him away, I say.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I warrant you, he will go with you of himself.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Yet more ado?

p.seg: I have made a fair mash of it.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Must I go?

div2.stage: [Enter DOCTOR Clement, Thorello, Lorenzo Sr., Bianca, Piso, Tib, [and] a Servant or two of the Doctor's.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Nay, but stay, stay. Give me leave. [To a Servant] My chair, sirrah. — You, Signor Lorenzo, say you went thither to meet your son?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Ay, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: But who directed you thither?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: That did my man, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Where is he?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Nay, I know not now. I left him with your clerk, and appointed him to stay here for me.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: About what time was this?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Marry, between one and two, as I take it.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: So, what time came my man with the message for you, Signor Thorello?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: After two, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Very good. — But lady, how that you were at Cob's, ha?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: An please you, sir, I'll tell you. My brother Prospero told me that Cob's house was a suspected place.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: So it appears, methinks. But on.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: And that my husband used thither daily.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: No matter, so he use himself well.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: True, sir, but you know what grows by such haunts oftentimes.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Ay, rank fruits of a jealous brain, lady. But did you find your husband there in that case, as you suspected?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: I found her there, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Did you so? That alters the case. Who gave you knowledge of your wife's being there?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Marry, that did my brother Prospero.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: How? Prospero first tell her, then tell you after? Where is Prospero?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Gone with my sister, sir, I know not whither.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, this is a mere trick, a device. You are gulled in this most grossly. [To Tib] Alas, poor wench, wert thou beaten for this? [Enter [a Servant], one of the Doctor's men. How now, sirrah, what's the matter?

sp.speaker: SERVANT
sp.p: Sir, there's a gentleman in the court without desires to speak with Your Worship.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: A gentleman? What's he?

sp.speaker: SERVANT
sp.p: A soldier, sir, he saith.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: A soldier? Fetch me my armor, my sword quickly! A soldier speak with me? Why, when, knaves? [He is brought armor, and arms himself.] Come on, come on, hold my cap there, so; give me my gorget, my sword. [To Lorenzo Sr., Thorello, and Bianca] Stand by. I will end your matters anon. [To the Servant] Let the soldier enter. [The Servant goes to the door.] [Enter Bobadilla and Matheo. Now, sir, what have you to say to me?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: By Your Worship's favor —

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To Matheo] Nay, keep out, sir, I know not your pretense. [To Bobadilla] You send me word, sir, you are a soldier. Why, sir, you shall be answered here; here be them have been amongst soldiers. Sir, your pleasure.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Faith, sir, so it is: This gentleman and myself have been most violently wronged by one Signor Giuliano, a gallant of the city here. And for my own part, I protest, being a man in no sort given to this filthy humor of quarreling, he hath assaulted me in the way of my peace, despoiled me of mine honor, disarmed me of my weapons, and beaten me in the open streets, when I not so much as once offered to resist him.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Oh, God's precious! Is this the soldier? [To the Servant] Here, take my armor quickly; 'twill make him swoon, I fear. He is not fit to look on't that will put up a blow.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: An't please Your Worship, he was bound to the peace.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, an he were, sir, his hands were not bound, were they?

sp.speaker: SERVANT
sp.p: There is one of the varlets of the city has brought two gentlemen here upon arrest, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Bid him come in. Set by the picture. [Bobadilla is led aside; the Servant goes to the door.] [Enter Musco [disguised as an arresting officer] with Giuliano and Stephano. Now, sir, what? Signor Giuliano? Is't you that are arrested at Signor Freshwater's suit here?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: I'faith, Master Doctor, and here's another brought at my suit.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To Stephano] What are you, sir?

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: A gentleman, sir. [Seeing Lorenzo Sr.] Oh, uncle!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Uncle? Who, Lorenzo?

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Ay, sir.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: God's my witness, uncle, I am wronged here monstrously! He chargeth me with stealing of his cloak, and would I might never stir if I did not find it in the street by chance.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Oh, did you find it, now? You said you bought it erewhile.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: And you said I stole it. Nay, now my uncle is here I care not.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Well, let this breathe a while. [To Bobadilla] You that have cause to complain there, stand forth. Had you a warrant for this arrest?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Ay, an't please Your Worship.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Nay, do not speak in passion so. Where had you it?

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Of your clerk, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: That's well, an my clerk can make warrants and my hand not at them! Where is the warrant? —Varlet, have you it?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: No, sir, Your Worship's man bid me do it for these gentlemen, and he would be my discharge.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, Signor Giuliano, are you such a novice to be arrested and never see the warrant?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Why, sir, he did not arrest me.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: No? How then?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Marry, sir, he came to me and said he must arrest me and he would use me kindly, and so forth.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Oh, God's pity, was it so, sir? He must arrest you? [To a Servant] Give me my long-sword there. Help me off, so. — Come on, sir varlet. [Musco kneels as Doctor Clement flourishes over him with his long-sword.] I must cut off your legs, sirrah. Nay, stand up; I'll use you kindly. I must cut off your legs, I say.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Oh, good sir, I beseech you! Nay, good Master Doctor. Oh, good sir!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: I must do it; there is no remedy. I must cut off your legs, sirrah; I must cut off your ears, you rascal, I must do it. I must cut off your nose; I must cut off your head.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Oh, for God sake, good Master Doctor!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Well, rise. [Musco rises.] How dost thou now? Dost thou feel thyself well? Hast thou no harm?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: No, I thank God, sir, and Your good Worship.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, so. I said I must cut off thy legs, and I must cut off thy arms, and I must cut off thy head, but I did not do it. So you said you must arrest this gentleman, but you did not arrest him. You knave, you slave, you rogue! Do you say you "must" arrest? [To a Servant] Sirrah, away with him to the jail! [To Musco] I'll teach you a trick for your "must."

sp.speaker: BRAINWORM
sp.p: Good Master Doctor, I beseech you, be good to me.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Marry o' God! Away with him, I say!

p.seg: Nay, 'sblood, before I go to prison, I'll put on my old brazen face and disclaim in my vocation. I'll discover, that's flat. An I be committed, it shall be for the committing of more villainies than this. Hang me an I lose the least grain of my fame!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, when, knave? By God's marry, I'll clap thee by the heels, too.

sp.speaker: BRAINWORM
sp.p: Hold, hold, I pray you!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What's the matter? [To the Servants] Stay there.

sp.speaker: BRAINWORM
sp.p: Faith, sir, afore I go to this house of bondage, I have a case to unfold to Your Worship. Which, that it may appear the more plain unto Your Worship's view, I do thus first of all uncase [Removing his disguise] and appear in mine own proper nature: servant to this gentleman [Pointing to Knowell Sr.] and known by the name of Musco.

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Ha? Musco!

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: Oh, uncle, Musco has been with my cousin and I all this day.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Did not I tell you there was some device?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Nay, good Master Doctor, since I have laid myself thus open to Your Worship, now stand strong for me till the progress of my tale be ended. And then if my wit do not deserve your countenance, 'slight, throw it on a dog and let me go hang myself.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Body of me, a merry knave! Give me a bowl of sack. [A Servant brings him drink.] Signor Lorenzo, I bespeak your patience in particular, marry, your ears in general. [He offers a toast to Musco.] Here, knave, Doctor Clement drinks to thee.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: I pledge, Master Doctor, an 'twere a sea, to the bottom.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Fill his bowl for that, fill his bowl. [Musco's cup is filled.] So, now speak freely.

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: [Drinking] Indeed, this is it will make a man speak freely. But to the point: know then that I, Musco, being somewhat more trusted of my master than reason required, and knowing his intent to Florence, did assume the habit of a poor soldier in wants. And, minding by some means to intercept his journey in the midway, 'twixt the grange and the city I encountered him. Where, begging of him in the most accomplished and true garb, as they term it, contrary to all expectation he reclaimed me from that bad course of life, entertained me into his service, employed me in his business, possessed me with his secrets — which I no sooner had received but, seeking my young master and finding him at this gentleman's house [Pointing to Prospero] , I revealed all most amply. This done, by the device of Signor Prospero and him together I returned (as the raven did to the ark) to mine old master again, told him he should find his son, in what manner he knows, at one Cob's house — where indeed he never meant to come. Now my master, he, to maintain the jest, went thither and left me with Your Worship's clerk, who, being of a most fine, supple disposition (as most of your clerks are), proffers me the wine which I had the grace to accept very easily, and to the tavern we went. There, after much ceremony, I made him drunk in kindness, stripped him to his shirt, and, leaving him in that cool vein, departed frolic, courtier-like, having obtained a suit. Which suit fitting me exceedingly well, I put on, and, usurping your man's phrase and action, carried a message to Signor Thorello in your name. Which message was merely devised but to procure his absence while Signor Prospero might make a conveyance of Hesperida to my master.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Stay. Fill me the bowl again. [His wine is replenished.] Here. 'Twere pity of his life would not cherish such a spirit! [To Musco] I drink to thee. [They drink.] Fill him wine. [To Thorello] Why, now do you perceive the trick of it?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Ay, I perceive well we were all abused.

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Well, what remedy?

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Where is Lorenzo and Prospero? Canst thou tell?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Ay, sir, they are at supper at the Mermaid, where I left your man.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To a Servant] Sirrah, go warn them hither presently before me, and, if the hour of your fellow's resurrection be come, bring him too. Exit Servant. [To Musco] But forward, forward. When thou hadst been at Thorello's —

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Marry, sir, coming along the street, these two gentlemen [Pointing to Bobadilla and Matheo] meet me, and, very strongly supposing me to be Your Worship's scribe, entreated me to procure them a warrant for the arrest of Signor Giuliano. I promised them upon some pair of silk stockings or a jewel or so to do it, and to get a varlet of the city to serve it; which varlet I appointed should meet them upon the Rialto at such an hour. They no sooner gone but I, in a mere hope of more gain by Signor Giuliano, went to one of Satan's old ingles, a broker, and there pawned your man's livery for a varlet's suit, which, here with myself, I offer unto Your Worship's consideration.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Well, give me thy hand. Proh superi! Ingenium magnum quis nosset Homerum, Ilias aeternum si latuisset opus ? I admire thee, I honor thee, and, if thy master or any man here be angry with thee, I shall suspect his wit while I know him for it. — Do you hear, Signor Thorello, Signor Lorenzo, and the rest of my good friends? I pray you, let me have peace when they come. I have sent for the two gallants and Hesperida. God's marry, I must have you friends. [A noise is heard.] How now? What noise is there?

sp.speaker: SERVANT
sp.p: Sir, it is Peto is come home.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Peto? Bring him hither, bring him hither. [Peto is brought forward.] What, how now, Signor Drunkard, in arms against me, ha? Your reason, your reason for this?

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: I beseech Your Worship to pardon me.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To the Servant] Well, sirrah, tell him I do pardon him.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Truly, sir, I did happen into bad company by chance, and they cast me in a sleep and stripped me of all my clothes.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Tut, this is not to the purpose. Touching your armor: what might your armor signify?

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: Marry, sir, it hung in the room where they stripped me, and I borrowed it of one of the drawers now in the evening to come home in, because I was loath to come through the street in my shirt.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [To the Servant] Well, disarm him. But it's no matter; let him stand by. [Peto is led to one side.] Who be these? — Oh, young gallants, welcome, welcome, and you, lady. Nay, never scatter such amazed looks amongst us. Qui nil potest sperare, desperet nihil .

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Faith, Master Doctor, that's even I; my hopes are small and my despair shall be as little. — Brother, sister, brother: what, cloudy, cloudy? "And will no sunshine on these looks appear?" Well, since there is such a tempest toward, I'll be the porpoise; I'll dance. [To Hesperida] Wench, be of good cheer; thou hast a cloak for the rain yet. Where is he? [To Lorenzo Jr.] 'Sheart, how now, the picture of the Prodigal? Go to, I'll have the calf dressed for you at my charges.

sp.speaker: LORENZO SR.
sp.p: Well, son Lorenzo, this day's work of yours hath much deceived my hopes, troubled my peace, and stretched my patience further than became the spirit of duty.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Nay, God's pity, Signor Lorenzo, you shall urge it no more. Come, since you are here, I'll have the disposing of all. But first, Signor Giuliano, at my request take your cloak again.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: [Taking his cloak] Well, sir, I am content.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Stay, now let me see. Oh, Signor Snow-Liver, I had almost forgotten him. And your Genius there, what, doth he suffer for a good conscience too? Doth he bear his cross with patience?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Nay, they have scarce one cross between them both to bear.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, dost thou know him? What is he? What is he?

sp.speaker: MUSCO
sp.p: Marry, search his pockets, sir, and they'll show you he is an author, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Dic mihi, Musa, virum . Are you an author, sir? Give me leave a little. Come on, sir. I'll make verses with you now in honor of the gods and the goddesses for what you dare, extempore. And now I begin:

lg.l: Mount thee, my Phlegon muse, and testify
How Saturn, sitting in an ebon cloud,
Disrobed his podex, white as ivory,
And through the welkin thundered all aloud.
There's for you, sir.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Oh, he writes not in that height of style.

lg.l: No? We'll come a step or two lower, then:
From Catadupa and the banks of Nile,
Where only breeds your monstrous crocodile,
Now are we purposed for to fetch our style.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Oh, too far-fetched for him still, Master Doctor.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Ay, say you so? Let's entreat a sight of his vein, then.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: [To Matheo] Signor, Master Doctor desires to see a sight of your vein. Nay, you must not deny him.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What, all this verse? Body of me, he carries a whole realm, a commonwealth of paper, in his hose! Let's see some of his subjects.

lg.l: [He reads] Unto the boundless ocean of thy beauty
Runs this poor river, charged with streams of zeal,
Returning thee the tribute of my duty,
Which here my youth, my plaints, my love reveal.

sp.p: Good! Is this your own invention?

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: No, sir, I translated that out of a book called Delia .

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Oh, but I would see some of your own, some of your own.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Sir, here's the beginning of a sonnet I made to my mistress.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: That, that. [He examines the dedication] Who? "To Madonna Hesperida." Is she your mistress?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: It pleaseth him to call her so, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: [Reads] "In summertime, when Phoebus' golden rays" — You translated this too, did you not?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: No, this is invention. He found it in a ballad.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Faith, sir, I had most of the conceit of it out of a ballad, indeed.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Conceit? [To a Servant] Fetch me a couple of torches, sirrah, I may see the conceit. Quickly; it's very dark.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Call you this poetry?

lg.l: Poetry? Nay, then call blasphemy religion,
Call devils angels, and sin piety;
Let all things be preposterously transchanged.
Why, how now, son? What, are you startled now?
Hath the breeze pricked you? Ha! Go to. You see
How abjectly your poetry is ranked
In general opinion.
Opinion? Oh, God, let gross opinion
Sink and be damned as deep as Barathrum!
If it may stand with your most wished content,
I can refel opinion and approve
The state of poesy, such as it is,
Blessd, eternal, and most true divine.
Indeed, if you will look on poesy
As she appears in many — poor and lame,
Patched up in remnants and old worn rags,
Half-starved for want of her peculiar food,
Sacred invention — then I must confirm
Both your conceit and censure of her merit.
But view her in her glorious ornaments,
Attird in the majesty of art,
Set high in spirit with the precious taste
Of sweet philosophy, and, which is most,
Crowned with the rich traditions of a soul
That hates to have her dignity profaned
With any relish of an earthly thought:
Oh, then, how proud a presence doth she bear!
Then is she like herself, fit to be seen
Of none but grave and consecrated eyes.
Nor is it any blemish to her fame
That such lean, ignorant, and blasted wits,
Such brainless gulls, should utter their stol'n wares
With such applauses in our vulgar ears,
Or that their slubbered lines have current pass
From the fat judgments of the multitude,
But that this barren and infected age
Should set no difference 'twixt these empty spirits
And a true poet — than which reverend name
Nothing can more adorn humanity.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Ay, Lorenzo, but election is now governed altogether by the influence of humor, which, instead of those holy flames that should direct and light the soul to eternity, hurls forth nothing but smoke and congested vapors that stifle her up and bereave her of all sight and motion. But she must have store of hellebore given her to purge these gross obstructions. [To the Servants] Oh, that's well said! Give me thy torch; come, lay this stuff together. So, give fire. [They burn Matheo's verses.] There, see, see, how our poet's glory shines brighter and brighter! Still, still it increaseth! Oh, now it's at the highest, and now it declines as fast. You may see, gallants, Sic transit gloria mundi . [To Bobadilla and Matheo] Well, now, my two Signor Outsides, stand forth and lend me your large ears to a sentence, to a sentence. First, you, signor, shall this night to the cage, and so shall you, sir. [To Matheo] From thence tomorrow morning, you, signor, shall be carried to the market cross and be there bound; [To Bobadilla] and so shall you, sir, in a large motley coat with a rod at your girdle. [To Matheo] And you in an old suit of sackcloth and the ashes of your papers — save the ashes, sirrah — shall mourn all day; and at night both together sing some ballad of repentance very piteously, which you shall make to the tune of "Who list to lead and a soldier's life." [To Peto] Sirrah billman, embrace you this torch and light the gentlemen to their lodgings, and, because we tender their safety, you shall watch them tonight; you are provided for the purpose. Away, and look to your charge with open eye, sirrah.

sp.speaker: BOBADILLA
sp.p: Well, I am armed in soul against the worst of fortune.

sp.speaker: MATHEO
sp.p: Faith, so should I be, an I had slept on it.

sp.speaker: PETO
sp.p: I am armed too, but I am not like to sleep on it.

p.seg: Oh, how this pleaseth me!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Now, Signor Thorello, Giuliano, Prospero, Bianca.

sp.speaker: STEPHANO
sp.p: And not me, sir?

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Yes, and you, sir. I had lost a sheep an he had not bleated. I must have you all friends. [To Prospero and Bianca] But first, a word with you, young gallant, and you, lady.

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Well, brother Prospero, by this good light that shines here, I am loath to kindle fresh coals, but, an you had come in my walk within these two hours, I had given you that you should not have clawn off again in haste. By Jesus, I had done it; I am the arrant'st rogue that ever breathed else! But now, beshrew my heart if I bear you any malice in the earth.

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: Faith, I did it but to hold up a jest and help my sister to a husband. But brother Thorello, and sister, you have a spice of the yealous yet, both of you — in your hose, I mean. Come, do not dwell upon your anger so much. Let's all be smooth-foreheaded once again.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: He plays upon my forehead, brother Giuliano. I pray you, tell me one thing I shall ask you: is my forehead anything rougher than it was wont to be?

sp.speaker: GIULIANO
sp.p: Rougher? Your forehead is smooth enough, man.

l.seg: Why should he then say 'Be smooth-foreheaded'
Unless he jested at the smoothness of it?
And that may be, for horn is very smooth;
So are my brows. By Jesu, smooth as horn!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: [To Prospero] Brother, had he no haunt thither, in good faith?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: No, upon my soul.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: [To Thorello] Nay then, sweetheart, nay, I pray thee, be not angry. Good faith, I'll never suspect thee any more. Nay, kiss me, sweet muss.

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Tell me, Bianca, do not you play the woman with me?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: What's that, sweetheart?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Dissemble.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Dissemble?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Nay, do not turn away. But say, i'faith, was it not a match appointed 'twixt this old gentleman [Pointing to Lorenzo Sr.] and you?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: A match?

sp.speaker: THORELLO
sp.p: Nay, if it were not, I do not care. Do not weep, I pray thee, sweet Bianca. Nay, so, now. By Jesus, I am not jealous, but resolved I have the faithfull'st wife in Italy!

lg.l: For this I find: where jealousy is fed,
Horns in the mind are worse than on the head.
See what a drove of horns fly in the air,
Winged with my cleansd and my credulous breath!
Watch them, suspicious eyes, watch where they fall:
See, see, on heads that think they have none at all!
Oh, what a plen'uous world of this will come!
When air rains horns, all men be sure of some.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, that's well. Come, then, what say you? Are all agreed? Doth none stand out?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: None but this gentleman [Pointing to Lorenzo Sr.] , to whom in my own person I owe all duty and affection, but most seriously entreat pardon for whatsoever hath passed in these occurrents that might be contrary to his most desired content.

lg.l: Faith, sir, it is a virtue that pursues
Any save rude and uncomposd spirits
To make a fair construction, and indeed
Not to stand off when such respective means
Invite a general content in all.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Well, then, I conjure you all here to put off all discontentment. First you, Signor Lorenzo, your cares; [To Thorello and Bianca] you and you, your jealousy; [To Giuliano] you, your anger; [To Prospero] and you, your wit, sir. And for a peace-offering, here's one willing to be sacrificed upon this altar. Say, do you approve my motion?

sp.speaker: PROSPERO
sp.p: We do. I'll be mouth for all.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Why, then, I wish them all joy. And now, to make our evening happiness more full, this night you shall be all my guests, where we'll enjoy the very spirit of mirth and carouse to the health of this heroic spirit [Indicating Musco] , whom to honor the more I do invest in my own robes, desiring you two, Giuliano and Prospero, to be his supporters; the train to follow. Myself will lead, ushered by my page here, with this honorable verse: Claudite iam rivos, pueri, sat prata biberunt .
